stem: The province is 120 km from Lito's house. He drove there at 60 km/h and drove back home on the same road at 40 km/h. What was his average speed for the whole round trip?
hints: Average speed is not the average of the two speeds. Use total distance ÷ total time.
Time going = 120 ÷ 60 hours. Time coming back = 120 ÷ 40 hours.
Add the two times. The total distance is 120 + 120. Divide the total distance by the total time.

steps.action: Let s = the average speed for the round trip, in km/h.
Time going: T = D ÷ R = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours.
Total time: 2 + 3 = 5 hours. Total distance: 120 + 120 = 240 km.
steps.why: A round trip means there and back, so the distance counts twice.

steps.action: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time: s = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/h.
steps.why: He drove longer at 40 km/h than at 60 km/h, so the average is closer to 40 than to 60.

steps.action: Check: 48 × 5 = 240 km, the whole round trip. His average speed was 48 km/h.

trapNotes.50 km/h: This averages the two speeds, (60 + 40) ÷ 2. He spent more time at the slower speed, so the true average is below 50. Use total distance ÷ total time.
trapNotes.24 km/h: This uses only one way: 120 km ÷ 5 hours. The round trip is 120 + 120 = 240 km.
trapNotes.100 km/h: This adds the two speeds. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
